Computational Consistency Validation

▼
Using two built-in validation samples (high/low risk each), compare web tree inference LP with R output to verify computational consistency (absolute error should be < 0.001).
Waiting for validation...
  1. This calculator is based on the GBM-Cox model (500 regression trees, shrinkage=0.05), developed with pure frontend HTML5 + JavaScript + Canvas, with all data processed locally;
  2. The income variable in the model has been inflation-adjusted to 2024 USD purchasing power; please adjust accordingly when inputting;
  3. The population average CSS survival curve is based on the SEER 2006–2020 bladder cancer training cohort of 76,942 patients, calculated at the average risk level (LP=0);
  4. 95% CI uses tree subsampling resampling (randomly selecting 90% of trees each time, repeated 100 times), approximate CI;
  5. This tool is for research use only and may provide quantitative reference for clinical decision-making, but does not replace professional medical judgment; individual actual survival may be affected by factors not included in the model.
